page.layout: Two parallel columns of a Hebrew-Latin lexicon: left column (Hebrew headword entries with Latin glosses and grammatical notes), then right column (continuing entries). Running head at top of each column, page number at top right. No margin notes, no text below the columns.

main_text.p: הוֹנָה, pro הוּנָה amotus fu-it, 2 Sam. 20. 13. præt. Hoph. 3. f. m. Rad. הָנָה.
הָנוּ pro הָגָה effari, Jer. 59.13. Inf. Kal, R. הָגָה.
הוֹנִיעַ fatigavit, הוֹנִיעוּ fatigavimus, הוֹנִיעָם fatigastis, הוֹנִיעֵנִי fatigasti me, הוֹנִיעֲךָ fatigatite, &c. 3. f. masc. 1. pl. 2. pl. m. 2. f. m. & 1. f. aff. Rad. יָנַע.
הוֹדָה celebravit, הוֹדוּ celebraverunt, הוֹדִינוּ celebravimus, præt. Hiph. 3. f. m. 3. pl. & 1. pl. item, הוֹדוּ celebrate, pl. m. Imper. Hiph. R. יָדָה.
הוֹרִיעַ notificavit, הוֹרִיעָה notificasti, הוֹרִיעוּ notificavimus, &c. 3. & 2. f. m. & 1. pl. præt. Hiph. Rad. יָדַע.
הוֹרִיעַ vel הוֹדִיעַ notifica; f. m. הוֹרִיעִי notificate, pl. m. Imper. Hiph.
הוֹדְךָ gloria tua, הוֹדֵךְ vel הוֹדוֹ ejus, No: Rad. הוֹד, aff.
הוֹדַע cognosci, הוֹדַעְתִּי me-um, Inf. Niph. aff. R. יָדַע.
הָוֶה existens, הָיָה e-sto, Job. 37.6. הֱיֵה esto, f. g. הָיָה erumna, הָיוֹת erumnæ, &c. vide in Rad. הָיָה.

הוֹחִיל expectavit, הוֹחִילוּ expectaverunt, הוֹחַלְתִּי expectavi, præt. Hiph. 3. f. m. 3. pl. & 1. f. ut הוֹחִיל expecta, f. g. הוֹחִילוּ expectate, Imper. Hiph. f. & pl. masc. & f. fem, Rad. יָחַל.
הוֹחַל captum est, 3. f. m. præt. Hoph. R. חָלַל.
הוּגְלָה deportatus est, deportati sunt, præt. Hoph. 3. f. m. & 3. pl. Rad. גָּלָה.

page.notes: Hebrew letters and vowel points are copied from a low-resolution scan and are doubtful throughout; the Latin is more reliable. Marked [?]: the running heads and page number (printed 7ı, read as 71), "notifica" and "notificate" (dotted and worn), "captum est" (the scan reads "teptum est", which is likely a damaged "captum"), and "deportatus" (partly obscured). The Hebrew transliterations in the left column near "הוֹנָה" and "הָנוּ" are uncertain. The right-column "sciens" line is partly obscured by an overlapping word.
